acquisition method: In this study, data‐dependent acquisition (DDA) was employed for all proteomic analysis.
cleavage agent: EVs total proteins were digested with trypsin (Promega, V5111), while glycoproteins were digested with trypsin and PNGase F (New England Biolabs, P0704)
enrichment method: lectin Concanavalin A (ConA) affinity chromatography; ZIC‐HILIC; Ti4+‐IMAC

N‐glycoproteins of 95C EVs and 95D EVs were extracted by lectin Concanavalin A (ConA) affinity chromatography; Intact glycopeptides were enriched via a ZIC‐HILIC (Merck) based solid‐phase extraction (SPE) method; Phosphorylated peptides were enriched by titanium (IV) ion immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography (Ti4+‐IMAC) material
fragmentation method: During HCD fragmentation, the N‐glycan core generates a series of Y‐type fragment ions
instrument: coupled with an Orbitrap Q‐Exactive Plus mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific); coupled with an Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
labeling: 2797 EVs total proteins were identified through label‐free quantitative proteomics
precursor tolerance: The mass tolerances for precursors and fragment ions were 6 ppm and 0.02 Da, respectively.
fragment tolerance: The mass tolerances for precursors and fragment ions were 6 ppm and 0.02 Da, respectively.
ptm: static: Cysteine carboxamidomethylation (C); variable: Oxidation on methionine (M); variable: deamidation (N and Q); variable: Methionine oxidation; variable: N‐terminal acetylation; variable: phosphorylation (pS/pT/pY)

Cysteine carboxamidomethylation (C) was set as a static modification. Oxidation on methionine (M) and deamidation (N and Q) with 0.984 Da mass increments were set as the variable modifications; Methionine oxidation, N‐terminal acetylation, and phosphorylation (pS/pT/pY) were set as variable modifications
